citation: Sobngwi E, et al. Fasting insulin sensitivity indices are not better than routine clinical variables at predicting insulin sensitivity among sub-Saharan Africans without diabetes. BMC Endocr Disord 2014;14:65.
protocol: Euglycaemic-hyperinsulinaemic clamp after 12 h fast: insulin primed over 10 min then 80 mU/m2/min for 100 min; blood glucose clamped at 5.5 mmol/L (100 mg/dl), checked every 5 min with 20% glucose; M over the final 20 min; OGTT also done (2 h glucose).
population: 87 non-diabetic Cameroonian volunteers (51 men, 36 women), age 21-61 y, screened healthy; table splits by sex and BMI category (lean to obese).

reports.marker: M value (mg/min/kg, unadjusted and per lean mass)

note: Sub-Saharan African data, rare among clamp papers. Only fasting values, 2 h glucose and M are printed, not clamp-state glucose or insulin; some obese subjects have 2 h glucose near 8 mmol/L, so read the lean/normal columns.
